newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks slip as markets await Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks slip as markets await Greenspan.

text.p: European stock markets retreated on Tuesday with central bank governors on both sides of the Atlantic stoking investors' anxiety over interest rates, while the dollar paused after its record-breaking runs.

Stock and foreign exchange markets were fixated by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and whether he would again try to trip up the raging bull on Wall Street when he testifies to the Senate at 1500 GMT.
"If Greenspan hints about higher interest rates today the bonds will take a big hit and shares could be in for a bumpy ride," said one London dealer.
Last December Greenspan sent shares reeling when he warned investors of irrational exuberance on financial markets. Dealers are now worried that he will stage a repeat performance.

"The last time he spoke he said the market was overheated and since then we've had a rise of another 500 points," said another London share dealer. "So he might well try to trip up that gigantic bull across the water."
Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 10.77 points on Monday at a record 6,843.87, seems to be losing its power to pull European markets up on its coat tails.
By late-morning on Tuesday London's FTSE index, which has hit a string of Dow-induced records since the New Year, was down 25 points at 4,169.0.
While investors can only guess what Greenspan will say, his British counterpart Eddie George has already rattled London.
British investors bought heavily last week when finance minister Kenneth Clarke left interest rates unchanged.

But the Bank of England governor, engaged in a tug of war with Clarke who has the final say on monetary policy, warned investors on Monday night that there were "real dangers" in letting sterling strength delay an interest rate rise.
His comments rekindled market speculation that interest rates could go up in early February even though Clarke is not keen on the idea before the general election due by May.
"Eddie George seems to be getting a little more strident in his views on interest rates," one trader said.
German stocks were equally weak, troubled again by Greenspan plus a domestic influence, this time an index from the IFO organisation indicating that the business climate remained soft.

In Frankfurt the DAX index slipped below the 3,000 barrier which it breached last week and by early afternoon it was down 50.50 points at 2,980.18. Dealers said that a long-awaited correction to the New Year bull run now seemed inevitable.
Paris followed the trend, with the CAC-40 index down 14.05 at 2,392.5.

But channel tunnel owner Eurotunnel extended Monday's 5.8 percent gain on higher 1996 revenues and prospects for completion of a bank debt accord by March. The share was up more than four percent at 7.55 francs.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar took a breather after hitting an almost four year high against the yen on Monday. Dealers awaited the highlight of the day: Greenspan.
"The trend is still for a higher dollar. What we've been seeing this morning is some profit-taking and readjustment ahead of Greenspan," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in London.

"I think the consensual view is that the Fed is not going to do anything to tighten monetary policy in February but that there will be tightening further down the road," said NatWest Markets currency strategist Kit Juckes.

The dollar was steady at 1.6230 marks compared with Monday's late European level of 1.6258. Against the yen it eased to 117.86 after breaching the the 118 barrier for the first time in almost four years on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was trading at 117.86 yen and 1.6230 marks compared with Monday's late European levels of 117.97 and 1.6258.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 25 points at 4,169.0
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was at 2,392.05, down 14.05. The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 50.50 at 2,980.18
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $353.65, compared with a $353.65 close in London on Monday. Silver was at $4.74 after closing Monday at $4.75. ($1=5.500 French Franc)
